$comment: eval_full_v2 — REVISED 2026-07-27. Two changes on top of the campaign that produced eval_full_v2_20260724-141520; every figure below is measured, not estimated (no-failure oracle LP, per-grid):
1. Every slack_budget_pct is raised to its grid's MEASURED minimum servable
value, so no grid sheds load in the no-failure baseline LP any more:
lv 0.50, lv_reconfig 0.50, lv_small unchanged, cp_dependent 0.50,
cp_heavy 0.55, cp_heavy_dependent 0.55, medium 0.95, mvlv 1.00.
Experiments spanning grids with different minima are split into one entry
per grid, keeping the experiment NAME so analysis still groups them.
CONSEQUENCE: the slack-budget sweep largely collapses (functional_baseline
on lv goes 0.30/0.45/0.60 -> 0.50/0.60; on medium all three -> 0.95), and
on medium/mvlv the budget is no longer a stress axis at all — those two
grids have almost no local supply (medium: 1 sgen at 6.5 kW vs 251 kW of
load; mvlv gas is single-fed), so 'servable baseline' and 'binding budget'
are mutually exclusive there.

CONSEQUENCE 2: the slack-budget levers lose their regime. just_slack_budget, sweep_slack and deadcheck_slack_target_fraction ran cp_heavy_dependent at 0.15 precisely because the budget bound there; at the servable minimum 0.55 it does not bind, so those three experiments now measure levers that cannot fire. Decide deliberately: keep them at 0.15 (accepting a 20 % pre-failure shed) or drop them.
NOT fixable by budget and deliberately left: line_stress electricity
(ampacity-limited, 0.805 at both 0.50 and 0.55), cold_day heat (0.666,
DHS transport under 1.5x load), and a 1-4 % residual heat gap on every
grid (McCormick-DHS / hydraulics).
2. New cp_necessity + just_cp_necessity pillars on two new grids where the
coupling points are actually load-bearing — see their $comment.
eval_full_v2 — the complete campaign. Composition:
base:   eval_full_recoverable.json (recoverable-loss pillars, line_stress split, 30-seed core)
merge:  eval_full.json scaling (4 grids incl. simbench_mvlv ~778 MES nodes) + ablation_reconfig (4-variant)
append: extension_campaign.json (islanding + temporal extensions)
append: eval_config_justification.json (per-lever justification: just_*/deadcheck_*/sweep_*)
dropped: cooldown_sweep (superseded by sweep_cooldown w/ target_metrics; ttl/community sweeps likewise superseded)
task_timeout_s=5400: extension_temporal (6 h physical horizon) and MVLV scaling tasks exceed the old 2400.
slurm mem=16G / time=02:00:00: islanding native-gurobi MILP and the 778-node MVLV grid need the headroom.
name: eval_full_v2

$comment: Bullet 1 headline — island self-anchoring, the ONLY recovery path
that converts disconnect_lost load back to SERVED (reconfig/coalition
only move loss into agent_shed). ENABLED 2026-07-07 after three fixes:
B) samplers were blind to GridForming* after microgrid promotion ->
0 failures; fixed in failure_sampling.py (now 1-2 island/seed).
A) infeasibility root-caused: promoted grid-formers had q_mvar_max=
0.1*p_max, too small for a severed island's reactive balance ->
every post-failure solve infeasible (IIS: island Q-balance vs gf
q_mvar). Fixed in modifiers.py (q_mvar_max=p_max). simbench_lv
8/8 seeds feasible; end-to-end 256/259->0 infeasible solves.
C) a mango async clock-freeze hang (one branch agent await across
the cut) was fixed separately; task now completes 109s, 0 failed.
DESIGN: paired microgrid-vs-clean A/B on IDENTICAL seeded cuts
(verified 6/6 seeds identical); only GF promotion differs, so the
delta isolates islanding. HEADLINE METRIC = the disconnect_lost ->
served shift (microgrid arm vs clean control), NOT the oracle gap:
scare>oracle in this regime (0.685>0.652) because the oracle min-shed
LP and scare min-de-energisation objective disagree on islanding, so
the oracle is NOT a valid ceiling here (open: characterise that
asymmetry). simbench_lv ONLY — medium still needs active headroom
(formulation forces e=1 at all GF buses); small untested.
experiments.name: recoverable_islanding

$comment: Bullet 1 (runnable) — FLISR / feeder-reconfiguration recovery.
simbench_lv_reconfig carries normally-open backup ties. A branch

forbids trivial external backfill so the reconfiguration decision is

$comment: Voltage-stress pillar — VDE-AR-N 4105 operating point.  Sunny midday: PV runs near nameplate while residential load drops to the morning trough, reversing feeder power flow.  ``vm_pu`` drifts toward the upper bound; without the Q-V droop the constraint monitor must shed real-power injection to recover (lost served energy).  With the droop, local Q absorption keeps voltage in deadband and full PV output is preserved.
Two-row ablation in a single experiment: scare-with-droop vs scare-without-droop on identical (grid, seed, scenario) — direct attribution of the droop's contribution.
experiments.name: voltage_stress

$comment: Line-loading stress pillar — exercises the line-thermal constraint pipeline.  Loads are scaled up 1.8x and every PowerLine's ampacity is halved, guaranteeing overload after a single branch failure redirects flow.  Three-row ablation in one experiment: full pipeline vs monitor-off vs reconfig-ranking-off — direct attribution of each new mechanism.

With the full pipeline: branch-mode monitor fires on overload, sends StartBalanceNegotiation to the lower-priority endpoint group, the reconfigurator's 6c ranking avoids the most-loaded restoration path.

Monitor-off baseline shows what the system does when line overload is silent (the legacy behaviour).  Ranking-off baseline tests whether the priority-aware shedding alone is enough without changing reconfiguration choices.
experiments.name: line_stress

$comment: Pillar 9 — CP flexibility shift.  The headline experiment for the cross-sector ADMM
layer.  Uses three new grid variants built with monee's cp_size_multiplier and
replace_primary_generation knobs:
cp_heavy_45            : CP rated output 2x, additive (loss of CP recoverable)
cp_dependent_45        : CP rated output 1x, replaces primary gen (loss of CP
disables BOTH the unit and the displaced primary gen)
cp_heavy_dependent_45  : both knobs combined (maximum cross-carrier dependence)
On the dependent variants, gossip + local-gen fallback alone cannot recover from a CP
failure because the displaced primary gen is gone — the cross-sector ADMM is
the only path to compensate.
Failures: generator-class so CPs themselves are part of the failure population.
experiments.name: cp_flexibility

cp_necessity
$comment: CP-NECESSITY pillar. The cp_*_dependent grids only SHIFT rated capacity into
the coupling points (9-18 % of the primary pool) and the operator slack
backfills the rest, so deactivating every CP in the no-failure LP costs
0.0001-0.0115 PWSF — less than the plain simbench_lv control (0.0074), and a
3-CP failure draw moves nothing at all (0.9951 -> 0.9947 on cp_heavy_dependent,
measured). These two grids make a carrier structurally unservable without its
converters. All figures below are the no-failure oracle LP, proven optimal
(Gurobi status 2, MIPGap 0), CPs-on vs all 47 CPs deactivated:
gas_dependent @0.40 (gas depends on power): gas has NO native production and
the budget covers only 40 % of gas demand; P2G synthesises the rest from
the surplus (1.5x) PV fleet. gas 1.000 -> 0.400 (= exactly the budget,
el_dependent @0.55 (power depends on gas): the PV fleet is cut to 20 %, so
the electrical balance closes only on CHP output, fuelled from gas.
MARGINAL SENSITIVITY (k random CP failures, the regime these scenarios sample):
gas_dependent loses ~2.7 pts of gas per failed P2G (k=1 0.972, k=2 0.946).
el_dependent absorbs CHP losses in HEAT, not electricity: the LP curtails
P2H (an electricity consumer) instead of shedding load, so el stays ~1.000
through k=3 while heat drops 0.988 -> 0.978. Electricity only breaks once the
fleet is gone. If marginal el sensitivity is wanted, cut chp_p_share to ~0.8
(or drop P2H from this grid and carry heat dependence on gas_dependent only).
Budgets are each grid's minimum servable value so the no-failure baseline is
NOT budget-limited and the whole gap is the converters. Failures are
generator-class so CPs are in the failure population.
Agent dropout robustness pillar — pending a mango scheduling hook for
mid-sim agent unregister.  Empty grids keep this entry as a placeholder.
experiments.name: robustness_dropout_TODO
experiments.notes: Pending: requires a mid-sim agent unregister mechanism in mango

experiments.$comment: Scenario row 1 = baseline (no islanding: sub-islands without a slack lose their load); row 2 = islanding extension + GridForming promotion. Same seeds and failure draws across rows. heat_mccormick on row 1 puts the clean arm on the SAME relaxed heat physics the microgrid arm needs for its MILP solve, so the paired delta isolates the islanding extension instead of confounding it with the heat relaxation.
experiments.name: extension_islanding

experiments.$comment: Scenario row 1 = multi-hour horizon WITHOUT temporal extensions; row 2 = same horizon with gas linepack + thermal LTC. Heat+gas generator failures + tight slack (0.15) put the deficit on the storage carriers. physics_time_scale=1 (sim clock = physical time), interval 10 => dt 10s, dur 21600 => 6h/2160 steps; sector_timescale sets physical control cadences (elec 30s, gas 120s, heat 600s poll). Periodic-only physics solving (ablation cooldown/max_acts) settles at converged agent states each step; stays feasible (0% solve fail) with PWSF flat vs coarser intervals — benchmarked ~7 min MAS / ~3 min oracle per task at 6h on the tiny LV-S (each MILP ~0.09s). Note interval < elec poll (30s) so physics updates faster than agents observe; finer than 30s only refines trajectory resolution. Tuned LV-S keeps the per-step solve cheap.
experiments.name: extension_temporal
experiments.$ablation_comment: physics_time_scale=1 makes the sim clock physical time; pair it with periodic-only physics solving (huge cooldown + max_acts=0) so the physics settles at CONVERGED agent states each 10-s step instead of re-solving mid-negotiation on every setpoint write — the latter caused ~27% infeasible-then-stale solves at the slow real-time cadence. Applies to both scenario rows and both variants, so no A/B confound.

experiments.$comment_block: L2 holonic / ADMM core. Concentrated-5 on simbench_lv drives a deep one-community deficit so holon redistribution, priority allocation, tier stratification, summary inversion-detection and the change-only cascade all fire. Metric: PWSF + priority-inversion count + churn/abandonment (NOT raw PWSF alone).
experiments.name: just_holonic_core

experiments.$comment_block: L1 gossip / sub-community dispatch, concentrated-5 deficit on lv_small. GRID CHOICE IS LOAD-BEARING: on simbench_lv the L1 gossip issues ZERO regulate writes (all dispatch flows through L2/L3; eval_smoke_v3 tasks 23 vs 25 were byte-identical), so gossip levers only bind on lv_small (balance-reason writes present). enable_qp_gossip OFF reverts to legacy equal-share; clpu_ramp OFF removes inrush throttling; modularity vs label-propagation changes partitioning. Metric: PWSF, share-stall events, ramp-violation, community-size dispersion.
experiments.name: just_gossip_l1

experiments.$comment_block: L3 cross-sector / CP layer. cp_heavy_dependent + generator failures + slack 0.15: restoration MUST flow through coupling points (the displaced primary gen is gone), the only regime where CP-ADMM, dynamic CP filtering, coalitions and heat->L3 supply have signal. Metric: served on dependent grid, cross-sector recovery, slack compliance.
experiments.name: just_cross_sector

experiments.$comment_block: Line-loading / curtailment pipeline. line_stress (load 1.8, ampacity 0.5) forces overload after a branch redirect, the only regime where the line monitor, constraint-aware gossip, multihop forwarding, auction + gating/targeting, reassert, branch-downstream relief and the reverse-priority waterfall all fire. Metric: line-loading violation integral, shed efficiency, priority-inversion under relief.
experiments.name: just_line_curtail

experiments.$comment_block: Voltage support. pv_peak on simbench_lv_small (the SMALL grid actually over-volts; the large grid never does) pushes vm_pu past the 1.03 deadband. Tests droop, VVW, the experimental auction-coordination hand-off + its feeder gate, the curtail-ramp interlock, recompute-on-failure and the end-of-sim settle tail. Metric: voltage-violation integral, over-voltage clear rate, PV curtailment, limit-cycle count.
experiments.name: just_voltage

experiments.$comment_block: Heat sector. cold_day (supply 343.15 K, heat load 1.5x) on cp_heavy forces a heat deficit so the frontier controller, tier waterfall, curtail-lock and heat->L3 CP supply link all have signal. Metric: heat served, heat priority-inversion, CP heat dispatch, heat curtail limit-cycle.
experiments.name: just_heat

experiments.$comment_block: Slack-budget enforcement + supply-utilisation levers. cp_heavy_dependent + generator failures + slack 0.15 makes the budget bind and the converter draw ride the slack. Tests the monitor, loss-compensating feedback, the OFF-by-default restore/serve-more + gen-ramp-to-full + nominal/cp-aware supply levers, and L2 generator ramp. Metric: slack-budget compliance, served, gen dispatch % and slack utilisation vs the oracle 100%/100%.
experiments.name: just_slack_budget

experiments.$comment_block: Gas pressure regulator. clean 4-failure on simbench_lv produces genuine gas under-pressure (de-energised ~0 cases are excluded at aggregation per DEENERGISED_PRESSURE_PU). Regulator walks the slack pressure_pu setpoint before shedding. Metric: genuine gas under-pressure task count + gas served.
experiments.name: just_gas_pressure

experiments.$comment_block: Reconfiguration ranking. simbench_lv_reconfig (5 backup branches/sector) + branch-4 failures give the path search alternatives to rank by peak loading. scare only: the reconfig oracle is a 15-binary MILP that times out (no S4 baseline) so variant comparison is excluded here. Metric: restored-path peak loading, served.
experiments.name: just_reconfig
